title: Radiation injury in rapidly renewing tissue
prompt: A 48-year-old patient develops mucosal inflammation during pelvic radiotherapy. In a laboratory model, injury to intestinal epithelial cells is reduced when a compound scavenging hydroxyl radicals is present during irradiation. Which initiating event best explains this protective effect?
options: Activation of a death receptor by a cytotoxic lymphocyte
explanation: Ionizing radiation can generate reactive species from water. Radical scavenging interrupts this indirect route of molecular damage; DNA can also be damaged directly.

distractorExplanations.Radiolysis of intracellular water: This generates reactive species that can injure DNA, proteins and membranes.
distractorExplanations.Activation of a death receptor by a cyto: Death-receptor signaling is an extrinsic apoptosis pathway, not the event directly blocked by a radical scavenger.
distractorExplanations.Failure of lysosomal acidification: Lysosomal acidification affects degradation but does not explain the immediate radiation-scavenging effect.
distractorExplanations.Accumulation of misfolded secretory prot: Misfolded proteins can trigger endoplasmic-reticulum stress; the experiment specifically implicates radicals.
distractorExplanations.Inhibition of the sodium-potassium ATPas: Pump failure explains cellular swelling after energy depletion, not the initiating radical-generating event.

title: Protein turnover during muscle wasting
prompt: A 63-year-old patient with advanced malignancy develops progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass despite nutritional support. Muscle cells are smaller, and studies demonstrate increased covalent attachment of a small regulatory protein to intracellular proteins before their degradation. Which system is most directly responsible?
explanation: Ubiquitin tagging can target proteins to proteasomes. Increased breakdown of cellular proteins contributes to muscle atrophy in catabolic states.

distractorExplanations.Ubiquitin-proteasome pathway: The ubiquitin tag directs selected proteins toward proteasomal degradation.
distractorExplanations.Caspase-mediated apoptotic fragmentation: Caspases participate in apoptosis, which involves cell dismantling rather than the described tagging of proteins in atrophic cells.
distractorExplanations.Complement membrane attack complex: Complement pores damage cell membranes and do not selectively tag intracellular proteins.
distractorExplanations.Lysosomal lipid storage pathway: Lipid storage reflects accumulation, not the described protein-targeting pathway.
distractorExplanations.Collagen cross-linking by lysyl oxidase: Collagen cross-linking concerns extracellular matrix maturation rather than intracellular muscle protein degradation.

title: Sequential antioxidant enzyme reactions
prompt: Following reperfusion of ischemic tissue, a researcher measures increased superoxide production. An enzyme preparation converts superoxide to hydrogen peroxide, but peroxide still accumulates unless a second detoxifying system is added. Which enzyme performs the first reaction?
explanation: Superoxide dismutase converts superoxide into hydrogen peroxide and oxygen. Catalase or glutathione peroxidase is needed for subsequent peroxide removal.

distractorExplanations.Catalase: Catalase removes hydrogen peroxide rather than producing it from superoxide.
distractorExplanations.Glutathione peroxidase: Glutathione peroxidase reduces peroxide using glutathione.
distractorExplanations.NADPH oxidase: NADPH oxidase generates superoxide in the respiratory burst.
distractorExplanations.Myeloperoxidase: Myeloperoxidase uses peroxide and chloride to generate hypochlorous acid.
